s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of throat fullness, pain, and respiratory distress with localized inflammation and mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue
salient_findings: Rapidly progressive fullness in the throat
Dyspnea with local redness at the root of the tongue
Non-homogeneous mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue
key_facts: Normal thyroid-stimulating hormone, triiodothyronine, and thyroxine levels
Flexible laryngoscopy showed a non-homogeneous, mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue
Neck ultrasound failed to identify the thyroid gland in its normal pretracheal location
Contrast-enhanced CT scan demonstrated a non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base
Peripheral calcifications and adjacent nodular structures enhanced similarly to thyroid tissue

shortlist.label: Lingual thyroid gland
shortlist.why_kept: Mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue and absence of thyroid gland in normal location

shortlist.label: Ectopic thyroid tissue
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of nodular structures enhancing similarly to thyroid tissue at the tongue base

shortlist.label: Base of tongue abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of throat fullness, pain, and fever with localized inflammation

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base with peripheral calcifications

shortlist.label: Retropharyngeal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Severe throat pain, dysphagia, and dyspnea with localized redness at the root of the tongue

raw.rationale: The presence of a non-homogeneous, mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue with peripheral calcifications and adjacent nodular structures that enhance similarly to thyroid tissue, combined with the failure to identify the thyroid gland in its normal pretracheal location, strongly suggests the presence of a lingual thyroid gland.

rejected.label: Ectopic thyroid tissue
rejected.why: While ectopic thyroid tissue could explain some findings, the specific location and characteristics described are more consistent with a lingual thyroid gland.

rejected.label: Base of tongue abscess
rejected.why: The absence of other signs of infection such as mucosal inflammation and the presence of calcifications and nodular structures that enhance like thyroid tissue make an abscess less likely.

rejected.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
rejected.why: Typically, thyroglossal duct cysts are midline and do not usually present with the complex imaging features described, such as peripheral calcifications and enhancement similar to thyroid tissue.

rejected.label: Retropharyngeal abscess
rejected.why: The location of the mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue and the specific imaging characteristics are not consistent with a retropharyngeal abscess.
